Recently I've read an article and discussed this article with a fellow student which had me thinking. The article stated that as the median age in Europe keeps rising it's a good idea to allow for young migrant workers. As you'll know the shrinking work force needs to pay more and more per capita in order to keep up the social benefits for pensionaries and sick citizens. Young migrant workers from Africa/Middle-east and Asia might be a solution to a problem. Speaking for my home country, The Netherlands this might certainly be a solution. But than again, for Spain and Portugal not so much, since their own youth is facing ridiculously high uneployment as is.

The solution I'd propose for The Netherlands is to allow migrant workers with reduced right to social benefits. When immigrants first arrive the public costs associated with them are very high, this is not something we should wish for in my opinion. Allowing them to migrate with reduced right to the social safety net in place reduces the public cost while maintaining the private benefits. This way we can still benefit from the advantages of labor migration(which according to most economists is always beneficiary to the economy as a whole) without it costing us too much. Of course, after a certain time period they would receive the right to full benefits.

But more questions arise with this solution, is it even ethical to treat immigrants as 'second-class citizens' and how do we 'prevent' aged immigrants or those who don't come here to work? I think this is an interesting concept and could be the solution to our ageing workforce problem while also solving the immigration crisis. What do you think voat?
Discussion: Europe should allow immigrants from an economic perspective

It seems like a good idea, but unless every European country joined in on this it could deter immigrants from countries that adopted this policy to instead go to countries that allow migrant workers full social rights immediately. If the EU or another primarily European supranational organization could get behind this, however, it could work.

No. People should be allowed in based on legal means.

They shouldn't let anybody in and risk letting in pedophiles, rapists, murderers, other criminals and even greater risk of letting in foreign terrorists without any problems.

You're going to cause a lot of problems from deaths, kidnappings and various of crimes by letting just anybody and everybody into the country.

Creating a lower class with racial/cultural bonds to one another that far outweigh the ones they have for their new country is probably a bad idea. You've already got a problem with homegrown jihadists. Having a sizable pool of immigrants whose sole purpose is working low-tier jobs and who have even less of a stake in society's function seems like a recipe for some bad shit.

As far as I know, instead of labelling them as "second-class citizens" you could implement an "intern ship program." You could have foreigners from developing countries have an occupation, learn from the experience and pass it on to their home country. Thus two parties benefit from this: the developed country and the under developed country.

So far I think the only European country to have a similar program is Sweden however I'll have to do further research on exactly what the government exactly does. A bad example would be Japan as the intern program has victimised very vulnerable people which has lead to massive slave labour from poor countries. Furthermore, those that are trapped are burdened in debt and seldom learn any valuable skills that could be used in their home country.

It's a good idea but it had to be properly regulated and hopefully will benefit both parties of the wealthy and the poor

At some point we're going to have to be able to sustain or economy and social programs without a growing population. Economic growth isn't a goal unto itself unless you're a major financial institution or a government, the average person is perfectly fine with slowed growth as long as their quality of life continues to improve.

Abolish the welfare state. That is the only answer in the end, and it would be better to just do it instead of trying to postpone the inevitable by inviting in an army of third world savages that will destroy European civilization.
